chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Whoever claims that God is from a thing, or in a thing, or upon a thing, has committed blasphemy.' I said, 'Explain it to me.' He said, 'I mean by the containment of the thing around Him, or by an attachment supporting Him, or from a thing that preceded Him.'

And in another report: 'Whoever claims that God is from a thing has made Him an originated being; whoever claims that He is in a thing has made Him contained; and whoever claims that He is upon a thing has made Him carried.'

key_terms.الْإِمْسَاكُ: Attachment, support, holding — the act of one thing being held in place by another; implies dependency
key_terms.الْحَوَايَةُ: Containment — the act of a thing surrounding and encompassing another; used here to explain what it would mean for God to be 'from' or 'in' a thing
key_terms.مَحْصُورٌ: Confined, contained, enclosed — an entity bounded within spatial limits
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ: Carried, borne, supported — an entity that requires another to sustain or carry it; implies creaturely dependency
key_terms.مُحْدَثٌ: Originated, created, contingent — an entity that came into existence after non-existence; the antithesis of the eternal

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq teach about the theological error of saying God is 'from,' 'in,' or 'upon' something?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a sweeping theological verdict: attributing to God spatial prepositions — 'from,' 'in,' or 'upon' — constitutes blasphemy (kufr), because each implies a limitation incompatible with divine transcendence. The Imam explains that 'from' implies God originated from a prior substance (making Him contingent), 'in' implies He is spatially contained, and 'upon' implies He requires support or a substrate. The second report makes this logic explicit: these three claims reduce God to a created, bounded, or carried entity — attributes belonging only to created things, not to the Necessary Being.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who claims that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is from a thing, or in a thing, or upon a thing, so he has Blasphemed’. I said, ‘Explain it to me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> mean by the emerging from the thing for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, of by the attachment to it, or from a thing preceding Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.

And in another report, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘The one who claims that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is from a thing, so he has Made Him<sup>azwj</sup> as an occurrence; and the one who claims that He<sup>azwj</sup> is in a thing, so he has Made Him<sup>azwj</sup> as contained; and the one who claims that He<sup>azwj</sup> is upon a thing, so he has Made Him<sup>azwj</sup> to be a Carried One’.
